_README: Hand-drafted distractor replacements for the gold72 items whose distractors are non-functional. Keys are item ids; 'distractors' replaces the three non-key options, the keyed answer text is never touched. Drafted from the BSB window text (see GOLD72_DISTRACTOR_REDRAFT_2026-09-12.md). Rules: every option comes from inside the item's own 3-verse window; same polarity; same syntactic shape and specificity; wrong-but-attractive, never near-correct. NAMES ARE CANONICAL -- the pseudonymized arm needs its own pass.

distractors: The altar was split apart
The ashes poured out from the altar
The king's hand withered
kcyl.note: all true events in v4-v6; only one follows the prayer, so the item now tests sequence

distractors: I cannot go home with you
You must not eat bread or drink water here
You must not return by the way you came
nntp.note: every option is speech in the window; only one is the prophet's -- tests speaker attribution

distractors: He tore down the walls of Gath and Ashdod
He was instructed in the fear of God by Zechariah
He built cities near Ashdod
tglh.note: key was the only positive among three negatives; all four now true, positive, in-window

distractors: Towers in the desert
Cisterns for his livestock
A fortified wall around the city
ryq4.note: all construction from v9-v10; the item now turns on WHERE

distractors: A great army appeared at their camp
They found the camp emptied at twilight
Their own horses and donkeys were taken
lxi8.note: key was the only auditory option; the first distractor reuses the verse's words but misattributes the modality

distractors: One of the centurions
A member of the Sanhedrin
The commander of the barracks
lik5.note: all four are people in the window; only one carries information TO Paul

distractors: He set up a shrine and made an ephod
He pays the Levite ten shekels a year
His mother dedicated the silver to the LORD
tyai.note: v13 is self-contained and 18:1-2 are a different scene, so these come from 17:3-17:10 -- OUTSIDE the window, which breaks rule 1. Either widen this item's window to 17:10-17:13 or drop it from the sensitivity set.

distractors: An ephod and household gods only
A graven image, a molten idol, and an ark
Household gods, a graven image, and silver
shz9.note: was tabernacle furniture and weapons; now partial/one-swapped versions of the real list -- tests enumeration

distractors: Gershom and his sons
Moses and his descendants
Micah and the young Levite
h3z1.note: the two new options are the other names in the SAME clause; answering requires parsing 'Jonathan son of Gershom, the son of Moses'

distractors: That they should rejoice in Abimelech
That fire would consume Beth-millo alone
That Abimelech would rule Shechem faithfully
iw06.note: the first is the BLESSING branch of the same if/if-not sentence (v19) -- forces tracking the conditional

distractors: Paul was guilty of treason
Paul should be exiled
Paul had already confessed to the charges
krfj.note: removes 'innocent of all charges' (0.55), which is a defensible paraphrase of the key

distractors: To test Abimelech's faith
To fulfill a prophecy
To reward Jotham for his warning
j38o.note: removes 'to punish the citizens of Shechem' (0.59), which v24 also supports

distractors: Four Philistine commanders.
Four champions from Gob.
Four soldiers from Jerusalem.
gphm.note: removes 'Four sons of David' (0.60), which the stem's own wording ('David and his servants') advertises
